fanout_allowlist.name: Explore
fanout_allowlist.rationale: Harness definition excludes Edit/Write/NotebookEdit; existing deep-explore fanout baseline (accepted exposure, not new attack surface); doubles as the planner agent (only research-capable entry).
fanout_allowlist.residual_risk: Has Bash — could theoretically mutate files or git state. Mitigated by prompt read-only contract + run-verify.js git-scoped checks (porcelain + tracked/untracked/ignored content hashes + tracked MODES + untracked/ignored directory nodes /refs/config/worktree/stash + .git/ hooks & info/exclude digest). tracked_modes_sha256 closes the tracked-permission bypass: git records only the exec bit, so `chmod 666` on a tracked file and `chmod 777` on a tracked directory left porcelain AND `diff HEAD` byte-identical -- a worker could make the whole tracked tree world-writable and the verifier reported no drift. untracked_dirs_sha256 closes the same hole for EMPTY untracked directories, which `status --porcelain -uall` never lists and the file-level enumeration only reaches through leaves. ignored_content_sha256 closes the gitignored-file bypass (a write to e.g. .env or a generated artifact is invisible to porcelain AND ls-files --exclude-standard). Out of v1 verification scope (v2 OQ): writes outside the repo; mutation of the EXCLUDED prefixes — control/safety plane (.claude_workflows/, .claude_review_state.json*, .claude_nit_history.json, .claude/cache/, .claude/worktrees/, .claude/jobs/) and high-volume dependency/build/cache trees (node_modules/ at any depth, .venv/, venv/, target/, build/, dist/, .gradle/, .next/) are omitted from the ignored-content hash; the control/safety-plane entries are ALSO filtered from the untracked-content hash, so a hook rewriting its own state plane in a consumer repo that does not gitignore it is treated identically on both sides (a sibling can still trip the unfiltered porcelain hash unless the shipped .claude_review_state.json* .gitignore glob is present); note stable ignored config like .claude/settings.local.json IS hashed; and index-mediated hiding of a tracked-file edit via `git update-index --assume-unchanged`/`--skip-worktree` (the edit then shows in neither `status --porcelain` nor `diff HEAD`, and the digest does not hash `.git/index`) — v2 must fold a stat-independent index digest in. (Packed-refs ref retarget/add/delete is already caught by refs_sha256's for-each-ref, so it is not a gap.) Also documented (near-zero, out-of-model): the untracked/ignored top-level CONTENT check uses `git hash-object`, which follows symlinks and has no --no-follow, so a classify(lstat isFile)->hash race repointing a regular path to a symlink-to-FILE within a single snapshot()/compare() call would hash the target -- unreachable while the verifier runs with no live fanout worker (SKILL.md ordering), fail-closed for symlink-to-directory, and self-drifting on the next non-raced snapshot; the directory branch (sha256File) and the .git-internals digest (hashRegularNodeNoFollow) already use object-identity O_NOFOLLOW+isFile reads. REMOTE side effects are likewise unverified and structurally invisible to run-verify.js, which observes only local repository state: the same generic Bash can drive an authenticated CLI (gh/aws/kubectl), curl, or `node -e` to mutate a remote system, and no local digest changes. Treat 'no external-write tool is declared' as 'not verified', not as 'proven zero' — closing it needs a network-disabled sandbox or removing generic-Bash workers from executable admission (v2).

explicit_exclusions.name: coverage-analyst
explicit_exclusions.reason: Bash(find:*) carries a write surface (-exec/-delete); verification-surface ⊇ attack-surface principle not satisfied for a new exposure.

explicit_exclusions.name: git-investigator
explicit_exclusions.reason: Bash(git:*) carries git write operations (tag/config/ref). run-verify.js refs/config hashes would detect them, but deny-by-default: new exposure without an existing fanout precedent is not worth the benefit. History archaeology runs as main-skill (/git-investigate) instead.
